headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: next-ai-draw-io can send document context to external APIs while transformers can read/write local files and execute code.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and draw.io XML and uses MCP plus browser-based AI assistance; transformers can consume stdin/stdout and files in pipeline workflows. A shared file or prompt bridge is plausible, so attacker-controlled document content from A could steer B. The exact bridge is undocumented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs untrusted document text into a shared workspace that agent_b reads
IF agent_b treats pipeline input as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Separate workspaces for A and B
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs by B
Add a prompt/content sanitizer before B
Require explicit human review of A-generated text before reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and has broad network egress to multiple third-party model APIs; transformers can read and write files and also has broad egress. If both touch the same documents, A may transmit sensitive file contents externally and B can further expose them through its own processing. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are opened in next-ai-draw-io
IF either agent forwards file contents to external inference APIs
mitigations: Use redacted copies of sensitive files
Restrict both agents to a local-only model endpoint
Block outbound traffic except approved hosts
Store API keys outside shared workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification gates

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad network egress, while transformers additionally has filesystem write, shell, and subprocess capabilities. They can contend for the same mutable files or model artifacts if co-located, but the profiles do not prove shared write targets or locking absence. That makes the conflict real but not clearly high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or project tree
IF shared model or diagram files are modified concurrently without locks
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Keep generated models and diagrams in distinct paths
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and transformers can act as a pipeline API over files and stdout. If B consumes A's generated text or diagram-derived facts without verification, errors can cascade into downstream outputs or actions. Because the profiles show a direct producer-consumer fit and no verification control, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative input
IF no human or programmatic verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Insert a validation step between A and B
Require citations or source links for A outputs
Compare A outputs against original files before use
Limit B to summarization, not action-taking
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff data

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source tools, but A explicitly handles API keys and sends data to multiple external AI providers, while B can also egress broadly. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for regulated documents even though no residency or certification data is stated. I cannot prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the higher justified choice.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is processed through either agent
IF outbound requests leave the operator's approved jurisdiction
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Use region-locked endpoints only
Disable external API calls for sensitive jobs
Log data flows for review
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
